critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge-Capital Augmented Book-to-Market
critic_notes.rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the published intangible-adjusted book-to-market / R&D-capital value factor (Lev–Sougiannis; Park 2019; Eisfeldt–Kim–Papanikolaou iHML), with no cross-theme content beyond the standard capitalization convention.

critic_notes.target_name: Intangible Value-Rank Repair Gap
critic_notes.rationale: The rank-wedge construction is a genuinely different object from either value level and is internally consistent, but it is close to a monotone re-labeling of R&D-stock-to-market (Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis), so the test must show it adds beyond that known predictor.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap and Productive Intangible Capital
critic_notes.rationale: Value-plus-turnover composites are a well-trodden value–quality combination, and dropping COALESCE means TS_SUM(xrd,5) is missing for the large non-R&D-reporting population, so coverage collapses to a selected subsample in a way the reasoning never acknowledges.

critic_notes.target_name: Enterprise Price per Intangible Dollar
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the reciprocal of the same intangible-adjusted valuation ratio already proposed (hence not an independent signal), and its denominator approaches zero for the many firms with negligible intan and R&D, guaranteeing unstable extreme-decile composition.

critic_notes.target_name: R&D Add-Back Earnings Yield
critic_notes.rationale: The signal is arithmetically E/P plus R&D-to-market, both individually documented predictors, so it is a trivial additive blend of known anomalies rather than a cross-theme interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Value Tilt Scaled by Intangible Intensity
critic_notes.rationale: The conditional shrinkage is correctly signed and the mechanism (adjustment matters only where intangibles are large) is coherent, but the stated claim of "without shrinking coverage" is false since TS_SUM(xrd,5) without COALESCE restricts the sample to five-year R&D reporters.

critic_notes.target_name: Hard-Book Value with Priced R&D Capital
critic_notes.rationale: Summing book-to-market with R&D-to-market is, up to the goodwill purge, exactly the published intangible-adjusted value / R&D-to-market anomaly pair (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis; Peters-Taylor), and it also collapses toward the archive's already-tested (ceq + R&D capital)/mktcap constructions, so it adds little beyond a rediscovery dressed as an ablation.

critic_notes.target_name: Hard-Book Value with Brand-and-Knowledge Share
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible one-dimension generalization of the winning conditioner that genuinely tests whether the effect is R&D-specific or a general expensing distortion, but the claim that missing xad means zero advertising is factually wrong (Compustat xad is overwhelmingly non-disclosure, not zero spend), so the perturbation may be mostly noise on a small subsample of disclosers.

critic_notes.target_name: Tangible-Only Book Value with Organic Knowledge Share
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate and interpretable ablation isolating goodwill-specific versus all-purchased-intangible contamination, though the proposal ignores that ceq − intan is frequently negative, which pushes acquisitive firms into a degenerate "expensive" tail and partly confounds the intended contrast.

critic_notes.target_name: Pre-Intangible Cash Yield on Enterprise Value
critic_notes.rationale: Cash-flow-to-enterprise-value is a well-documented standalone value anomaly (enterprise multiple, CF/P) with the R&D add-back a minor known refinement, so this is barely cross-theme; moreover the stated claim that enterprise value is always positive and tail-safe is false for net-cash firms, where the ratio flips sign.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapness with Productive Total Intangible Capital
critic_notes.rationale: This is a substantively motivated response to the diagnosed level-versus-trend failure of the gen-0 efficiency signal, and grossing up the profitability denominator by unrecorded knowledge capital is a real twist on standard value-plus-gross-profitability, but the assertion that the denominator is a sum of positive quantities is wrong since ceq can be negative and will produce exploding tails.

critic_notes.target_name: Acquired-Intangible Overhang in Expensive Stocks
critic_notes.rationale: ADD(gdwl, intan) double-counts goodwill because Compustat intan already includes it, so the second leg is not the intended construct, and the signal is otherwise largely a sign-flipped restatement of the winner's short leg combined with the known goodwill/intangible-intensity underperformance result.

critic_notes.target_name: EBITDA Yield with Organic Knowledge Share
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible anchor swap that trades a book-based for a flow-based cheapness measure at higher coverage, though it is incremental relative to the existing oancf-anchored gen-1 signal, and the hypothesis is loosely worded (EBITDA is itself reduced by expensed R&D, which arguably strengthens rather than bypasses the mechanism).

critic_notes.target_name: Dual-Anchor Cheapness with Unrecorded Capital Share
critic_notes.rationale: Averaging hard-book B/M with sales-to-price is a reasonable consolidation and correctly diagnoses that the gen-0 failure came from multiplicative shrinkage, but both anchors share the same market-cap denominator so the claimed noise diversification is limited and the incremental content over the existing winner is modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Builders Versus Cheap Buyers of Intangible Capital
critic_notes.rationale: The organic-minus-acquired rank difference makes an economically real distinction that is only implicit in the incumbent conditioner, is internally consistent with the expected positive sign, and is constructed to avoid the 0/0 degeneracy of a direct share ratio.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapness with Persistent Innovation Record
critic_notes.rationale: TS_COUNT(xrd,5) is largely a Compustat reporting-convention indicator that collapses to a near-binary "is an R&D firm" dummy, so it both conflates disclosure with economics and overlaps heavily with the incumbent conditioner (which is already ~0 for non-reporters), leaving little independent variation among genuine innovators.

critic_notes.target_name: Within-Industry Hard-Book Value and Knowledge Share
critic_notes.rationale: Industry-demeaning both legs of the existing winning signal is a standard robustness transformation rather than a new mechanism, and while the sector-tilt-versus-firm-mispricing diagnostic is genuinely informative, it is a cosmetic variant of the archived gen-0 composite rather than a substantive refinement.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Firms Shifting from Acquired to Organic Intangibles
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the gen-1 "Innovation Outsourcing at Rich Prices" signal with the sign flipped and the three components reweighted — the same economic content (organic-versus-purchased intangible growth interacted with valuation) — so it risks being a rediscovery, even though the reweighting is motivated by a plausible CMA-loading diagnosis.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Self-Funded Builders of Brand and Knowledge
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical stack of two already-tested conditioners (gen-1 brand-and-knowledge share, gen-2 net cash) on the unchanged hard-book anchor, with no new mechanism and an undiscussed nested-SUMRANK weighting (50% value, 25% each conditioner) that makes any incremental result uninterpretable relative to its two parents.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Knowledge Firms with Unlevered Balance Sheets
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping net cash for pure leverage is only a leg substitution, but it is a genuinely diagnostic decomposition of the gen-2 funding-capacity result and is economically motivated (non-collateralizable knowledge capital plus offsetting the value leg's distress loading), so it is worth one test.

critic_notes.target_name: Unmonetized Pipeline with Financing Slack
critic_notes.rationale: Another two-conditioner stack, but the horizon (R&D/revenue) and survivability (net cash) legs are conceptually orthogonal rather than two intensity proxies, so the joint test carries some information beyond its parents — though it should be judged only against the 5.6% and 7.3% parent alphas, not against zero.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Firms Shrinking Their Acquired Intangibles
critic_notes.rationale: NEG(ΔGoodwill/at) is close to a goodwill-restricted asset-growth/acquirer-underperformance signal already partly spanned by CMA and by the archive's gen-1 goodwill-change signal, its expected positive sign sits awkwardly against published post-impairment underperformance, and the huge mass point at Δgdwl = 0 (all non-acquirers) makes the conditioner rank largely degenerate so the composite will be driven by the value leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Intensity Versus Premium Over Hard Book
critic_notes.rationale: The stated motivation is internally inconsistent — replacing enterprise value with market cap *introduces* rather than removes leverage contamination (levered firms mechanically get a low ME/at and hence a high signal) — and what remains is essentially R&D intensity plus a book-to-market proxy, i.e. a scaling variant of the gen-0 signal and of the well-known R&D-adjusted value effect.

critic_notes.target_name: Smoothed Cheapness with Organic Knowledge Share
critic_notes.rationale: A three-year moving average of the incumbent's value leg is a cosmetic timing variant, not a substantive mechanism change, and with annual accounting data it mostly injects stale prices (mixing in 2-3 year-old momentum/reversal information) rather than cleanly separating persistent undervaluation from a recent price collapse.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapness with Innovation Load on Gross Profit
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical recombination of two archived components — the gen-1 WINSOR(xrd/gross profit) conditioner bolted onto the already-heavily-reused hard-book anchor — and the conditioner itself is the fourth near-monotone rescaling of R&D intensity (after xrd/(ceq+xrd), xrd/revt, xrd/(cogs+xrd)), so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism, even if the coverage diagnostic is honest.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators Penalized for Leveraged Knowledge
critic_notes.rationale: The reframing of financing risk as an interaction penalty rather than a third additive rank is a substantively different construction with a coherent collateral-value story, but the claim that a rank product bounded in [0,1] "cannot dominate" the ranked core is wrong — the penalty has comparable dispersion to the SUMRANK core and may convert the signal into a leverage×R&D short bet, which should be checked with a leg-decomposition.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators Penalized for Unstable Revenue
critic_notes.rationale: Revenue-growth volatility is a genuinely new conditioning dimension for this archive and the paired financial-vs-fundamental-fragility diagnostic is well motivated, though it partially rides the known fundamental-volatility/low-risk anomaly and inherits the same unverified claim that the bounded rank product will not overwhelm the value core.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Within-Industry Innovation Leaders
critic_notes.rationale: Industry-demeaning only the intangible leg is a clean, well-posed test of whether the archive's winners are competitive-positioning effects or a pharma/software sector tilt, and the outcome is interpretable and actionable either way despite the construction being simple.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash-Adjusted Cheapness of Knowledge Firms
critic_notes.rationale: The economic reinterpretation of net cash as measurement error in the value ratio is legitimate, but the expression is fragile exactly where the hypothesis bites — cash-rich innovators can have che exceeding market cap and/or hard book, producing negative or near-zero denominators and sign-flipped ratios that will dominate the extremes of the cross-section — and it is also close to a standard enterprise-value/net-cash-adjusted book-to-market construction.

critic_notes.target_name: Jointly Cheap and Knowledge-Intensive
critic_notes.rationale: This is the gen-0 archive winner with MIN substituted for SUMRANK on identical legs — a functional-form tweak of an existing signal rather than a new hypothesis — and the archive already showed MIN degrades performance while heavily compressing and tying the cross-section.

critic_notes.target_name: Tangible Book Cheapness with Brand and Knowledge Share
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two already-archived gen-1 variants (intan-purged book anchor and the xrd+xad organic conditioner), each of which already delivered ~6.4-6.6% alpha with t≈5, so the combination is a cosmetic consolidation that is very unlikely to yield new economic information beyond the parents.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators with Cash Priced In
critic_notes.rationale: Rescaling net cash by market cap makes the conditioner share the same 1/P denominator as the hard-book value leg, so the "repair" mechanically reloads the composite on cheapness/size rather than isolating the financing-slack channel, and any fmb improvement would be uninterpretable.

critic_notes.target_name: Total Intangible Pipeline per Revenue Dollar
critic_notes.rationale: A clean single-design-change test of whether the unmonetized-pipeline conditioner generalises from R&D to total organic intangible spend, internally consistent and correctly signed, though incremental and dependent on the sparse, COALESCE-zeroed xad field which may make it near-identical to its R&D-only parent.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Firms Whose Losses Are R&D-Induced
critic_notes.rationale: A genuinely new mechanism for this archive — a discrete accounting-classification boundary rather than a continuous intensity conditioner — with the indicator pair correctly encoding "loss that disappears when R&D is added back," though the SUMRANK combination is additive rather than the claimed conditional gating and the binary leg will produce coarse, tie-heavy ranks over a narrow subsample.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators Whose Knowledge Is Converting
critic_notes.rationale: The diagnosis that level gross profitability is spanned by RMW while its three-year change is not is economically sensible and motivates a substantively different leg, but gross-profit growth is close to the established profitability-growth anomaly and GROWTH on a base that can be near zero or negative will be noisy even after ranking.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators That Also Distribute Cash
critic_notes.rationale: The dividend-yield leg is both a well-known standalone value anomaly and, like the net-cash-over-price proposal, shares the 1/P denominator with the value anchor, so the composite double-counts cheapness; the large mass of zero-dividend innovators also makes the conditioner nearly a non-payer dummy rather than a graded revealed-preference measure.

critic_notes.target_name: Unmonetized Pipeline in Net-Creditor Innovators
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally coherent and correctly signed, but it is a 2×2 recombination of two archived parents that already deliver 7.5% and 7.7% alphas with near-identical legs, so it is a cosmetic swap of a continuous slack measure for its own binary indicator rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Hard-Book Value Plus Net Hidden Capital
critic_notes.rationale: SUMRANK of (ceq−gdwl)/P and (xrd5−intan)/P is, up to the rank transform, just the intangible-adjusted book-to-market that the archive already tested repeatedly (gen-0 repair gap, gen-3 "Cheap Under Both Conventions") and that the published intangible-value literature owns, and the defense that sharing the 1/P denominator "is the point" concedes the two legs are near-collinear valuation ratios rather than distinct channels.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators with Rising Gross Profitability
critic_notes.rationale: Replacing GROWTH(gross profit,3) with DELTA(GP/AT,2) is a defensible functional-form and coverage repair of an archived 6.8%-alpha signal with a correctly signed conversion story, though it remains a variant rather than a new mechanism and the claim that a profitability *change* escapes RMW's span is an assertion the test will have to settle.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Stock Priced Below Half of Market Value
critic_notes.rationale: The conditioner is a hard-coded threshold on cumulative R&D-to-market, which is the classic Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis R&D/market-cap anomaly in coarsened form, and the 0.5 cutoff is arbitrary and will select a small, distress-tilted tail of beaten-down biotech-type microcaps whose behavior is driven by price collapse rather than by any accounting-state mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Dual-Anchor Cheapness in Solvent Knowledge Firms
critic_notes.rationale: This is a four-way equal-weighted ensemble of already-evaluated archive components with no new economic content; blending a high-fmb anchor with a high-alpha anchor will mechanically produce intermediate statistics on both metrics, which cannot distinguish a genuine frontier from simple averaging.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators Still at Peak Commitment
critic_notes.rationale: The asymmetric distance-from-running-maximum is a genuinely distinct decay concept and not the gen-2 mean-deviation surprise, but the stated construction claim is wrong — because the leg is weakly negative by construction, COALESCE-zero non-R&D firms score at the *maximum* of that leg and are pushed toward the long side rather than "the neutral middle," which contaminates the conditioner and must be fixed before the test is interpretable.

critic_notes.target_name: Brand-and-Knowledge Cheapness in Net-Creditor Firms
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's already-evaluated "Cheap Innovators That Are Net Creditors" with the R&D share swapped for the equally already-evaluated xrd+xad share — a cosmetic two-leg recombination explicitly motivated by picking the fmb-leader and alpha-leader rather than by any new economics.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapness in Doubly Favorable Accounting States
critic_notes.rationale: The conjunction of two indicators is a marginally different construction than a rank average, but both states are already in the archive and the resulting conditioner is a coarse 0/1/2 variable whose flagged population (R&D stock above hard book *and* net cash) is likely dominated by small, cash-rich micro-innovators, so it mostly re-slices existing evidence.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Innovators with Expanding Gross Margin
critic_notes.rationale: This is the third implementation of the same "conversion" conditioner (after GROWTH of gross profit and DELTA of gross profit/assets), differing only in the scaling denominator, which is exactly the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Firms Investing in Knowledge Not Assets
critic_notes.rationale: The intangible-versus-tangible investment substitution conditioner is a genuinely new construction for this archive and internally consistent, but its short-side driver is essentially the canonical asset-growth anomaly (already partly spanned by CMA), so incremental alpha over the existing builders-versus-buyers and non-dilution variants is uncertain, and the claim that "any incremental alpha must come from the intangible side" is not established.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapness Graded by Accounting Conservatism
critic_notes.rationale: The signed goodwill-heavy short state is a worthwhile new addition, but the stated hypothesis (cheapness "informative in one regime, meaningless in another") requires an interaction while the expression merely adds a ternary state to the B/M rank, so the construction does not implement the mechanism claimed.

critic_notes.target_name: Self-Built and Unlevered Versus Bought and Borrowed
critic_notes.rationale: Summing goodwill and total debt into one asset-scaled term is an arbitrary fusion of two already-tested conditioners with no clear reason the two should carry equal weight, and the proposal itself concedes the likely outcome is the average of its parents.

critic_notes.target_name: Three-Year Knowledge Share with Hard-Book Cheapness
critic_notes.rationale: This is a pure lookback-window tweak (5→3 years) of the archived "Hard-Book Cheapness with Organic Knowledge Share," i.e., a parameter variant with no new economic content, and the R&D-stock depreciation-rate question is itself a well-trodden calibration issue rather than a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Economic Equity Above Market Value
critic_notes.rationale: Algebraically this is (hard book + R&D stock)/at minus market-cap/at, so it is dominated by the ordinary market-to-assets term — a rescaling of the well-known (intangible-adjusted) book-to-market anomaly rather than a new construct — and the reasoning's claim that the difference is "bounded" is simply false, since market cap per dollar of assets is unbounded above and will dominate the cross-sectional variation.

critic_notes.target_name: Brand-and-Knowledge Cheapness with Funding Runway
critic_notes.rationale: Internally coherent and correctly signed, but it is a mechanical stacking of two already-archived winners (brand-and-knowledge share, gen-1; innovation runway, gen-7) with the same nested-SUMRANK weighting the archive has used repeatedly, so the likely outcome — modestly higher alpha with a diluted Fama-MacBeth slope — is the already-documented three-leg pattern rather than new information.

critic_notes.target_name: Conditioner-Weighted Cheapness in Solvent Innovators
critic_notes.rationale: Duplicating the knowledge-share leg inside a nested SUMRANK purely to change its implicit weight is a cosmetic re-weighting of two existing parents with no new economic mechanism, and the motivation — recovering fmb without losing alpha — is explicitly curve-fitting to prior evaluation statistics.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Acquisition-Free Innovators
critic_notes.rationale: The indicator logic is correct (NEG(gdwl/at) > −0.05 does isolate low-goodwill firms) and the joint "no acquired intangibles, meaningful organic R&D" state is a defensible discrete refinement, though it is economically close to the archived "Cheap Builders Versus Cheap Buyers" signal and the binary conditioner will create heavy ties in the second SUMRANK leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Regime-Signed Cheap Innovator Composite
critic_notes.rationale: The gating indicator (R&D stock > hard book) is close to a mechanical restatement of the composite's own knowledge-share leg (share > ~0.5), so multiplying one by the other is largely self-referential rather than an independent regime test, and the construction is otherwise a direct core-swap variant of the archived gen-7 "Cheapness Gated by Accounting Regime."

critic_notes.target_name: Restated Cash Yield in Rollover-Safe Innovators
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two already-evaluated archive signals (gen-8 pre-innovation cash-earnings yield + knowledge share, and gen-8 hard-book with the che>dlc rollover state) with no new construct, and since both legs are already measured the outcome is a predictable interpolation rather than a test of a new mechanism.

critic_notes.target_name: Fully Restated Intangible Cash Yield and Share
critic_notes.rationale: The internal-consistency argument — the same organic intangible spend defined in both the flow numerator and the capital-share conditioner — is the one genuinely principled construction in this batch, though be aware that xad is missing for most firms (COALESCE to zero) and that both legs load positively on xrd, pushing the composite toward the known R&D-to-market anomaly rather than a distinct effect.

critic_notes.target_name: Stock and Flow Cheapness Both Restated
critic_notes.rationale: Averaging two anchors that share the same market-cap denominator and have each already been tested with the identical conditioner will almost certainly land between their known results (alpha 6.1%/fmb 4.4 and alpha 4.4%/fmb 7.7), so this is a cosmetic blend rather than a test of the claimed fmb-alpha "frontier."

critic_notes.target_name: Cheap Firms with Research-Induced Negative Cash Earnings
critic_notes.rationale: The state is the same mechanism as the archive's gen-5 "Cheap Firms Whose Losses Are R&D-Induced" with the profitability line swapped from ib to ebitda, which is close to a cosmetic variant, and the narrower EBITDA-negative-but-EBITDA+R&D-positive condition will concentrate the long leg in tiny pre-revenue biotech names, raising instability rather than sharpening the mechanism — the expression itself is internally consistent with the hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Restated Cash Yield with Unmonetized Pipeline
critic_notes.rationale: Coherent and correctly signed, but it is another cell in an already-mapped 2x2 of archive anchors and conditioners (pre-innovation yield × pipeline/revenue), and the "both are income-statement quantities" rationale is a presentational point rather than an economic reason to expect a different result.

critic_notes.target_name: Brand-and-Knowledge Cheapness Safe From Rollover
critic_notes.rationale: All three legs — hard-book cheapness, the brand-inclusive organic share, and the che>dlc indicator — are already individually evaluated in the archive, and the stated motivation is inconsistent with the construction since a soft SUMRANK tilt does not "exclude" term-financed firms, so nothing about the long-term-debt-aversion diagnosis is actually being tested.
